chunks.arabic_text: اَلْكَافِي: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ، عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ، عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ

translations.en: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Sama'a ibn Mihran, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قُلْتُ: أَصْلَحَكَ اللَّهُ، إِنَّا نَجْتَمِعُ فَنتَذَاكَرُ مَا عِنْدَنَا، فَلَا يَرِدُ عَلَيْنَا شَيْءٌ إِلَّا وَعِنْدَنَا فِيهِ شَيْءٌ مَسْطُورٌ، وَذَلِكَ مِمَّا أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ بِهِ عَلَيْنَا بِكُمْ، ثُمَّ يَرِدُ عَلَيْنَا الشَّيْءُ الصَّغِيرُ لَيْسَ عِنْدَنَا فِيهِ شَيْءٌ، فَيَنْظُرُ بَعْضُنَا إِلَى بَعْضٍ، وَعِنْدَنَا مَا يَشْبَهُهُ، فَنُقِيسُ عَلَى أَحْسَنِهِ؟

translations.en: I said: May Allah make you prosper, we gather and discuss what we have (from you), nothing is referred to us except that we have something recorded regarding it, and that is from what Allah has blessed us with through you; then a small matter may be referred to us in which we have nothing (recorded), so we look at one), so we look at one another, and we have something similar to it, should we analogize it to the best (closest scenario)?

chunks.arabic_text: فَقَالَ: وَمَا لَكُمْ وَالْقِيَاسِ؟ إِنَّمَا هَلَكَ مَنْ هَلَكَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ بِالْقِيَاسِ،

translations.en: He said: And what do you have to do with analogical reasoning? Verily they were destroyed those who were destroyed before you because of analogical reasoning,

chunks.arabic_text: ثُمَّ قَالَ: إِذَا جَاءَكُمْ مَا تَعْلَمُونَ، فَقُولُوا بِهِ، وَإِنْ جَاءَكُمْ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ، فَهَمَّ (وَأَهْوَى بِيَدِهِ إِلَى فِيهِ)،

translations.en: Then he said: If it comes to you that which you have knowledge of, then say it; and if it comes to you that which you do not know, then be silent (and he pointed with his hand to his mouth),

chunks.arabic_text: ثُمَّ قَالَ: لَعَنَ اللَّهُ أَبَا حَنِيفَةَ، كَانَ يَقُولُ: قَالَ عَلِيٌّ وَقُلْتُ أَنَا، وَقَالَتِ الصَّحَابَةُ وَقُلْتُ أَنَا،

translations.en: Then he said: May Allah curse Abu Hanifa, he used to say: 'Ali said but I say,' and 'The Companions said but I say,'

chunks.arabic_text: ثُمَّ قَالَ: أَكُنْتَ تَجْلِسُ إِلَيْهِ؟ قُلْتُ: لَا، وَلَكِنْ هَذَا كَلَامُهُ،

translations.en: Then he said: Did you use to sit with him? I said: No, but these are his words,

chunks.arabic_text: قُلْتُ: أَصْلَحَكَ اللَّهُ، أَتَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ النَّاسَ بِمَا يَكْتَفُونَ بِهِ فِي عَهْدِهِ؟

translations.en: I said: May Allah make you prosper, did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) come with all that which would suffice them (the people) in his time?

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ: نَعَمْ، وَمَا يَحْتَاجُونَ إِلَيْهِ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ، قُلْتُ: فَضَاعَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ شَيْءٌ؟

translations.en: He said: Yes, and even that which they will have need of up to the Day of Judgment, I said: Has anything from that been lost?
He said: No, it is with his family.

en.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) advises his followers to rely on recorded narrations rather than analogical reasoning (qiyas), which he claims caused the destruction of previous nations. He instructs them to speak what they know and remain silent (pointing to the mouth) when they do not know, criticizing Abu Hanifa's method of appending 'but I say' to the statements of Ali and the Companions. He confirms that the Prophet brought sufficient guidance and that nothing has been lost, as it remains with the Ahl al-Bayt.
en.seo_question: What is the Shia view on analogical reasoning (qiyas) and how does it differ from relying on the Ahl al-Bayt?

key_terms.الْقِيَاس: Analogical reasoning (qiyas), a method of deriving legal rulings by comparing a new case to an existing one based on a common cause.
key_terms.أَهْلِهِ: His family, referring specifically to the Ahl al-Bayt (the Prophet's family and Imams) who are the custodians of the divine knowledge.
key_terms.مَسْطُورٌ: Recorded or written down, referring to the preserved narrations and traditions.
key_terms.أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ: Abu Hanifa, the founder of the Hanafi school of Sunni jurisprudence, criticized here for his method of appending his own opinion to the statements of the Imams and Companions.
